projects.label: Open-world detection
projects.title: Open-world object detection
projects.line: A YOLOv8 detector that flags what it doesn't recognise as UNKNOWN, so a person can review it and the model can learn from the correction.
projects.problem: A standard detector only knows its training classes, so anything new gets a wrong label instead of a flag. On an aquarium marine-animal dataset, an unfamiliar animal is named incorrectly rather than set aside.
projects.approach: Detect with YOLOv8, treat low-confidence detections as UNKNOWN, and send those to a Streamlit screen where a person relabels them. The corrections become data for incremental retraining.
projects.challenge: Deciding where known ends and unknown begins. Confidence is only a proxy, so the threshold controls how much work reaches the reviewer.

projects.label: Notebook RAG
projects.title: Notebook RAG
projects.line: A modular RAG application: document extraction, chunking, embeddings, vector search and retrieval, with a chat history store.
projects.problem: Answering questions from your own documents takes more than a prompt. The text has to be extracted, split, embedded and searched first.
projects.approach: Separate modules for extraction, chunking, embedding, vector storage and retrieval, with Gemini, Cohere and OpenRouter clients and a store for chat history.
projects.challenge: Keeping each stage separate enough to test, since the repo has a tests folder, while the whole pipeline still works as one app.

projects.label: Research agent

projects.approach: A Python agent built with LangGraph concepts, as a trial of what I'd learnt so far.
